---
title: "Landing page"
---

The [landing page](https://scilifelab-training.github.io/scilifelab-training-template/)
is the front door of your training. It introduces the training as a
whole, and helps visitors decide whether to register, or which training
instance to open.

The figure below shows the parts of the landing page, and the names this
guide uses for them.

![](images/landing-01-overview.png){width=75% fig-alt="Annotated example of the landing page showing the template banner, training title and subtitle, logos, hero buttons, information cards, the All training instances banner with its image, and the footer."}

In this chapter, you will learn how to:

- [Switch off template mode](#switch-off-template-mode)
- [Change the title and subtitle](#change-the-title-and-subtitle)
- [Add or remove logos](#add-or-remove-logos)
- [Edit the information cards](#edit-the-information-cards)
- [List your training instances](#list-your-training-instances)
- [Set up the hero buttons](#set-up-the-hero-buttons)
- [Change the banner image](#change-the-banner-image)
- [Edit the footer](#edit-the-footer)

### Before you start {.unnumbered}

Everything in this chapter happens on the **main** branch, and almost
all of it in the four data files in the `data` folder:

| Data file | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `data/course.yml` | The title, description, learning outcomes, keywords and topics of your training |
| `data/team.yml` | The people behind the training |
| `data/instances.yml` | The list of training instances |
| `data/website.yml` | Logos, button texts, the banner image and the footer |

: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}  
  
Work as described in [Regular workflow](workflow.qmd): start the
preview with `python scripts/preview.py`, make your changes, save them, and check
them in your browser. You don't have to commit after every change:
you can make several changes, and commit and push them together.

If you're not sure how a data file works, see
[Data files](repository-structure.qmd#data-files).

At the end of the chapter, a **cheat sheet** box sums up which
file to open and what to change. It is handy when you come back to the
guide later.


## Switch off template mode {#switch-off-template-mode}

Your repository starts as a copy of the template, so it still presents
itself as the template. You can see this in the yellow
 **Want to use this template?**  banner at the top of the landing page (see overview image above).
Switching off **template mode** turns your repository into your own
training. Do this first:

1. On the **main** branch, open `data/website.yml`.
2. Find the line:

   ```yaml
   template: true
   ```

3. Change it to:

   ```yaml
   template: false
   ```

4. Save the file (Cmd+S (macOS) or Ctrl+S (Windows and Linux))

This changes two things:

- The yellow banner disappears from the landing page.
- The README, `CITATION.cff` and `.zenodo.json` now describe **your**
  training, using your data files. While template mode was on, they
  described the template itself.

::: {.done}
**Done when:** the yellow banner is gone from the preview.
:::

### Replace the README {.unnumbered}

Your repository's README, the description shown on its main page on
GitHub, still describes the template. Replace it with the README for a
training:

1. In the Explorer panel, open the `docs` folder and then
   `_template-README.md`.
2. Select all text (**Cmd+A** or **Ctrl+A**) and copy it.
3. Open `README.md` in the main folder of your repository, select all
   text, and paste, so the copied text replaces it.
4. Delete the note at the top of the file, between `<!--` and `-->`,
   and the line starting with `> **Template:**`.
5. Fill in the parts marked **Write this yourself**. The other parts,
   between `<!-- generated:... -->` lines, are filled in automatically
   from your data files.
6. Save the file.


## Change the title and subtitle {#change-the-title-and-subtitle}

The **hero** is the large dark banner at the top of the landing page. It
is the first thing visitors see, and shows the title and subtitle of
your training, the logos and the buttons.

1. Open `data/course.yml`.
2. Find the lines:

   ```yaml
   title: "Training title"
   subtitle: "Training subtitle"
   ```

3. Replace the text between the quotation marks with the title and
   subtitle of your training.
4. Save the file.

The title is also used as the title of your website in the browser tab,
in the README and in the citation of your training.

::: {.callout-tip}
Keep the subtitle to one sentence, and start it with an action verb such
as **Learn**, **Understand**, **Explore**, **Build** or **Apply**. For
example:

> *Learn how to apply open science practices throughout the research
> lifecycle.*

The subtitle is optional: to leave it out, change it to `subtitle: ""`.
:::

## Add or remove logos {#add-or-remove-logos}

The logos in the hero show the organisations behind your training. You
can add logos, remove them, or replace them with your own.

### Add a logo {.unnumbered}

1. Save your logo as an **SVG** or **PNG** file.

   ::: {.callout-tip}
   Use a **white** version of your logo, or one made for a dark
   background, so it stands out against the dark hero.
   :::

2. Copy the file into the `img/logos` folder: drag it from your
   computer onto the folder in the Explorer panel in VS Code.
3. Open `data/website.yml` and find the `hero` part:

   ```yaml
   hero:
     logos:
       - src: "img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
         alt: "SciLifeLab"
   ```

4. Add your logo at the bottom of the list. Copy the two lines of an
   existing logo, from `- src:` to `alt:`, and paste them below. Then
   change the values:
   - `src`: where the file is, starting with `img/logos/`, followed by
     the file name;
   - `alt`: the name of the organisation. Screen readers read this out
     for visitors who can't see the logo.

   For example:

   ```yaml
   hero:
     logos:
       - src: "img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
         alt: "SciLifeLab"
       - src: "img/logos/my-organisation.svg"
         alt: "My organisation"
   ```

5. Save the file.

The logos appear in the same order as in the list.

::: {.callout-note}
Keep the spaces at the start of each line exactly as in the example: the
`- src:` line of every logo starts at the same position, and `alt:`
lines up with `src:`.

The file name in `src` must match the name of your file exactly,
including capital letters and the extension (`.svg` or `.png`).
:::

### Remove a logo {.unnumbered}

1. Open `data/website.yml` and find the `hero` part.
2. Delete both lines of the logo you want to remove: the `- src:` line
   and the `alt:` line below it.
3. Save the file.
4. Optional: if you no longer need the logo file, delete it from the
   `img/logos` folder. In VS Code, right-click the file and choose
   **Delete**.


## Edit the information cards {#edit-the-information-cards}

The **information cards** below the hero describe your training. They
are created from your data files:

| Card | Comes from |
|---|---|
| **Training content** | `description` in `data/course.yml` |
| **Learning outcomes** | `learning_outcomes` in `data/course.yml` |
| **Keywords** | `keywords` in `data/course.yml` |
| **Topics covered** | `topics` in `data/course.yml` (optional) |
| **Founders** | People with the role `Founder` in `data/team.yml` |
| **Contributors** | People with the role `Contributor` in `data/team.yml` |

: {tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

The same information is also used in the README and the citation of
your training, and helps people find it in Zenodo and training
registries such as TeSS.

### Training content {.unnumbered}

1. Open `data/course.yml` and find `description`:

   ```yaml
   description: |
     Description of the content of the training.

     Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit...
   ```

2. Replace the example text below `description: |` with a description
   of your training. Keep the two spaces at the start of every line.
   Separate paragraphs with an empty line.

The `|` after `description:` lets you write several lines and
paragraphs. You can also use simple formatting, such as `**bold**` or
links: `[link text](https://example.org)`.

::: {.callout-tip}
Focus on what the training covers. Around ten sentences is usually
enough.
:::

### Learning outcomes, keywords and topics {.unnumbered}

These three are **lists**: each line starting with `-` is one item.

1. Open `data/course.yml` and find `learning_outcomes`, `keywords` or
   `topics`:

   ```yaml
   learning_outcomes:
     - "Learning outcome 1"
     - "Learning outcome 2"
     - "Learning outcome 3"
   ```

2. Replace the example text between the quotation marks with your own.
3. To **add** an item, copy a whole line, paste it below, and change
   the text. To **remove** an item, delete its whole line.

The learning outcomes are numbered automatically on the website.

::: {.callout-tip}
- **Learning outcomes** describe what participants will be able to do
  after the training. For guidance, see the
  [SciLifeLab Training Hub resources on writing learning outcomes](https://figshare.scilifelab.se/articles/educational_resource/Training_Hub_Resources_for_Learning_Outcomes/28473218).
- **Keywords**: around four or five short terms that describe the main
  subject areas. They help people find your training.
- **Topics**: short phrases, not full sentences, that give visitors a
  quick overview of what the training covers.
:::

The **Topics covered** card is optional. To leave it out, replace the
list with an empty one:

```yaml
topics: []
```

### Founders and contributors {.unnumbered}

The **Founders** and **Contributors** cards list the people in
`data/team.yml`:

- **Founders** started the training, or are responsible for it.
- **Contributors** contributed materials or expertise.

Each person looks like this:

```yaml
- given_names: "Firstname1"
  family_names: "Lastname1"
  roles:
    - Founder
  affiliation: "Institution or organisation"
  orcid: ""
  citation_author: true
```

1. Open `data/team.yml`.
2. Fill in the details of each person:
   - `given_names` and `family_names`: first name(s) and surname. Put
     words like "van der" in the surname.
   - `roles`: `Founder` or `Contributor`.
   - `affiliation`: the organisation the person works for.
3. To **add** a person, copy a whole entry, from `- given_names:` to the
   last line before the next `- given_names:`, paste it below, and
   change the values. To **remove** a person, delete their whole entry.

Each card is left out when nobody has that role. The other fields, such
as `orcid`, `email`, `course_contact` and `citation_author`, are used
for the citation of your training. They are explained in
[FAIRification](fairification.qmd) and in the comments at the top of
`data/team.yml`.

::: {.callout-important}
Every person needs `given_names`, `family_names`, `roles` and
`affiliation`. If one is missing, the preview shows an error that names
the person and the missing field.
:::

## List your training instances {#list-your-training-instances}

The **All training instances** banner near the bottom of the landing
page has a button for each training instance. Visitors use it to open
the website of the current training, or of an earlier one.

The list comes from `data/instances.yml`. Each training instance looks
like this:

```yaml
- slug: "2605"
  label: "May 2026"
  status: current
  visible: true
  show_in_hero: true
  instance_url: "./2605/"
  registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
  sort_key: 202605
```

| Field | What it means |
|---|---|
| `slug` | The year and month of the training instance as YYMM, the same as in its branch name. For example, `"2605"` for the branch **release-2605** |
| `label` | The text on the button, for example `"May 2026"` |
| `status` | `current` for the training instance that is running now or coming up next; `previous` for earlier ones |
| `visible` | `true` to show the button in the banner; `false` to hide it |
| `show_in_hero` | Only for the current training instance: whether the hero shows a button to it. See [Set up the hero buttons](#set-up-the-hero-buttons) |
| `instance_url` | The link to the website of the training instance: `"./YYMM/"`, with the same digits as `slug` |
| `registration_url` | Only for the current training instance: the link to its registration page |
| `sort_key` | The year and month as YYYYMM, for example `202605`. Used to put the training instances in order |

: {tbl-colwidths="[25,75]"}

::: {.callout-important}
- Exactly **one** training instance has `status: current`. All others
  have `status: previous`.
- The current training instance always has `visible: true`.
- Each training instance has its own `slug`: never use the same one
  twice.
- `slug` and `instance_url` use the same four digits.

If one of these rules is broken, the preview shows an error that
explains what to fix.
:::

### Remove the example training instances {.unnumbered}

The template's list contains example training instances, such as
**2505** and **2411**, that don't exist in your repository. Their
buttons would lead to pages that don't exist. Start by removing them:

1. Open `data/instances.yml`.
2. Delete the whole entry of each example instance, from `- slug:` to
   `sort_key:`, except the one with `slug: "0000"`.
3. Save the file.

Keep the **0000** entry for now: it links to the example training
instance on the **release-0000** branch. You replace it once your first
own training instance is ready.

### Add a training instance {.unnumbered}

Each training instance has its own **release-** branch, with its own
website. Adding it to `instances.yml` puts a button to that website on
the landing page.

::: {.callout-note}
Creating a **release-** branch does **not** add it to this list
automatically. First create the branch, as described in
[Training instances](training-instances.qmd), and then add it here.
:::

1. Open `data/instances.yml`.
2. Copy a complete entry, from `- slug:` to `sort_key:`, and paste it at
   the top of the list, directly under `instances:`.
3. Change `slug`, `label`, `instance_url` and `sort_key` to the new
   training instance.
4. If the new training instance is now the current one, see
   [Change the current training instance](#change-the-current-training-instance)
   below.
5. Save the file.

For example, for a training instance in November 2026:

```yaml
- slug: "2611"
  label: "November 2026"
  status: current
  visible: true
  show_in_hero: true
  instance_url: "./2611/"
  registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
  sort_key: 202611
```

::: {.callout-note}
Keep the spaces at the start of each line exactly as in the existing
entries: `- slug:` is indented by two spaces, and the other lines of
the entry by four.
:::

### Change the current training instance {#change-the-current-training-instance .unnumbered}

When a new training instance becomes the current one:

1. In `data/instances.yml`, find the training instance that is current
   now, and change its `status` and `show_in_hero`:

   ```yaml
   status: previous
   show_in_hero: false
   ```

2. Find the new current training instance, and set:

   ```yaml
   status: current
   visible: true
   show_in_hero: true
   ```

3. Save the file.

For example:

```yaml
instances:

  - slug: "2611"
    label: "November 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2611/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202611

  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: previous
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: false
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: ""
    sort_key: 202605
```

### Show or hide an earlier training instance {.unnumbered}

You may not want to show every earlier training instance on the landing
page. To hide one, set its `visible` to `false`:

```yaml
visible: false
```

To show it again, set it back to `true`. A hidden training instance
stays in the list, and its website stays online: only its button
disappears from the banner.

::: {.callout-warning}
Never hide the **current** training instance with `visible: false`. To
remove its button from the hero, use `show_in_hero: false` instead. See
[Set up the hero buttons](#set-up-the-hero-buttons).
:::

### Change the text on a button {.unnumbered}

Change the `label` of the training instance, for example from
`"May 2026"` to `"Spring 2026"`. This only changes the text visitors
see, not where the button leads.

### Change the order {.unnumbered}

The current training instance is always shown first. The earlier ones
follow, newest first, sorted by `sort_key`. You don't need to put the
entries in order yourself, as long as each `sort_key` is the year and
month of its training instance, written as YYYYMM: for example,
`202605` for May 2026.


## Set up the hero buttons {#set-up-the-hero-buttons}

The hero can show two buttons:

- **Take me to the current instance** opens the website of the current
  training instance.
- **Register now** opens the registration page of the current training
  instance.

Both buttons use the training instance with `status: current` in
`data/instances.yml`. See
[List your training instances](#list-your-training-instances) to set
which one that is.

### Add the registration link {.unnumbered}

1. Open `data/instances.yml` and find the training instance with
   `status: current`.
2. Replace the example link in `registration_url` with the link to your
   registration page or form:

   ```yaml
   registration_url: "https://your-registration-page.example"
   ```

3. Save the file.

### Hide the registration button {.unnumbered}

When registration has closed, or your training doesn't need
registration, empty the link of the current training instance:

```yaml
registration_url: ""
```

The **Register now** button disappears. To show it again, fill in the
link again.

### Hide the current instance button {.unnumbered}

When there is no current training instance to point to, for example
when your training is self-paced or not given at the moment, set
`show_in_hero` of the current training instance to `false`:

```yaml
show_in_hero: false
```

The button disappears from the hero. The training instance stays in the
**All training instances** banner.

### Change the button texts {.unnumbered}

You can change the text on the buttons, and the heading of the
**All training instances** banner, without changing where they lead:

1. Open `data/website.yml` and find the `labels` part:

   ```yaml
   labels:
     hero_view_current_label: "Take me to the current instance"
     hero_registration_open_label: "Register now"
     instances_band_title: "All training instances"
   ```

2. Change the text between the quotation marks. For example:

   ```yaml
   hero_view_current_label: "Go to the latest training"
   hero_registration_open_label: "Sign up"
   ```

3. Save the file.

## Change the banner image {#change-the-banner-image}

The **All training instances** banner shows a decorative image next to
the buttons. You can replace it with an image that fits your training.

1. Copy your image into the `img/images` folder: drag it from your
   computer onto the folder in the Explorer panel in VS Code.

   ::: {.callout-tip}
   Use a landscape image. The image is cropped automatically to fill
   the space, so keep the important part near the middle.
   :::

2. Open `data/website.yml` and find:

   ```yaml
   instances_band:
     image: "img/images/navet-band.png"
   ```

3. Replace `navet-band.png` with the file name of your image, for
   example:

   ```yaml
   instances_band:
     image: "img/images/my-training-banner.jpg"
   ```

4. Save the file, and check the preview at different widths of your
   browser window.

To show no image at all, set `image: ""`.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Is the important part of your image cut off?

You can choose which part of the image stays visible. This is the only
change in this guide in `styles.css`, the file that controls the look of
the website, so make it carefully:

1. Open `styles.css` and search for `.instances-band__image`
   (**Cmd+F** or **Ctrl+F**).
2. In that block, find:

   ```css
   object-position: center;
   ```

3. Change `center` to the part you want to keep. For example,
   `center top` keeps the top of the image, and `30% center` moves the
   visible part to the left.
:::


## Edit the footer {#edit-the-footer}

The **footer** at the bottom of the landing page shows who runs the
training, its licence, how the website was built, and a link to your
repository on GitHub. All of it is in the `footer` part of
`data/website.yml`.

### Organisation {.unnumbered}

Change `organisation` to the name of the organisation, programme or
group responsible for your training:

```yaml
organisation: "SciLifeLab Training Hub"
```

### Licence {.unnumbered}

The licence tells others how they may reuse your training. The footer
shows its name, linked to the page that explains it:

```yaml
licence:
  name: "CC BY 4.0"
  url: "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
```

::: {.callout-important}
The licence also appears in `reuse` in `data/course.yml`, where it's
used for the README and the citation. If you choose another licence,
change it in **both** files, so they say the same, and replace the text
in `LICENSE.md`. See [FAIRification](fairification.qmd) for help
choosing a licence.
:::

### Repository link {.unnumbered}

The GitHub logo in the footer links to your repository. Replace `url`
with the address of your repository on GitHub:

```yaml
repository:
  url: "https://github.com/your-organisation/your-repository"
  image: "img/logos/Github_Neg.png"
  alt: "GitHub repository"
```

You find the address in your browser's address bar when you open your
repository on GitHub, for example
`https://github.com/SciLifeLab-Training/introduction-to-r`.

::: {.callout-important}
The repository link is **required**. The template also uses it to work
out the address of your website, for the citation of your training.
:::

### Built with {.unnumbered}

The `built_with` part credits the SciLifeLab Training Webpage Template.
You can usually leave it as it is.

## Cheat sheet {#cheat-sheet}

All changes on the landing page, on one screen. Everything happens on
the **main** branch.

### Template mode {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Switch off template mode and remove the banner | `data/website.yml` | Set `template: false` |

### Title and subtitle {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Change the title | `data/course.yml` | The value of `title` |
| Change the subtitle | `data/course.yml` | The value of `subtitle` |
| Leave out the subtitle | `data/course.yml` | Set `subtitle: ""` |

### Logos {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Add a logo file | `img/logos/` | Copy your logo (`.svg` or `.png`) into the folder |
| Show a logo | `data/website.yml` | Add `- src:` and `alt:` lines under `hero:` → `logos:` |
| Remove a logo | `data/website.yml` | Delete the `- src:` and `alt:` lines of the logo |
| Delete an unused logo file (optional) | `img/logos/` | Delete the file |

### Information cards {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Change the training content | `data/course.yml` | The text below `description: \|` |
| Change the learning outcomes | `data/course.yml` | The list under `learning_outcomes` |
| Change the keywords | `data/course.yml` | The list under `keywords` |
| Change the topics | `data/course.yml` | The list under `topics` |
| Leave out the topics card | `data/course.yml` | Set `topics: []` |
| Add or change founders and contributors | `data/team.yml` | Add or edit a person, with `roles` set to `Founder` or `Contributor` |

### Training instances {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Remove the example training instances | `data/instances.yml` | Delete their entries, except `"0000"` |
| Add a training instance | `data/instances.yml` | Copy an entry to the top of the list and change `slug`, `label`, `instance_url` and `sort_key` |
| Change the current training instance | `data/instances.yml` | Old one: `status: previous` and `show_in_hero: false`. New one: `status: current`, `visible: true` and `show_in_hero: true` |
| Hide an earlier training instance | `data/instances.yml` | Set `visible: false` |
| Change the text on a button | `data/instances.yml` | Change `label` |
| Change the order | `data/instances.yml` | Set `sort_key` to the year and month, as YYYYMM |

### Hero buttons {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Add the registration link | `data/instances.yml` | `registration_url` of the current training instance |
| Hide the registration button | `data/instances.yml` | Set `registration_url: ""` for the current training instance |
| Hide the current instance button | `data/instances.yml` | Set `show_in_hero: false` for the current training instance |
| Change the button texts | `data/website.yml` | `hero_view_current_label` and `hero_registration_open_label` under `labels` |
| Change the heading of the banner | `data/website.yml` | `instances_band_title` under `labels` |

### Banner image {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Add your image | `img/images/` | Copy your image into the folder |
| Use your image | `data/website.yml` | `image` under `instances_band` |
| Show no image | `data/website.yml` | Set `image: ""` |
| Adjust the cropping (optional) | `styles.css` | `object-position` in `.instances-band__image` |

### Footer {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| To... | File | What to change |
|---|---|---|
| Change the organisation | `data/website.yml` | `organisation` under `footer` |
| Change the licence | `data/website.yml` and `data/course.yml` | `licence` under `footer`, and `licence` under `reuse`. Also replace `LICENSE.md` |
| Link to your repository | `data/website.yml` | `url` under `footer` → `repository` |



## Next steps {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Your landing page now describes your training. Continue with:

- [Training instances](training-instances.qmd): create the website for
  each time your training is given.
- [FAIRification](fairification.qmd): make your training citable and
  findable.
